---
title: "Writing a shorter account"
subtitle: "Examine what a generated summary preserves and changes"
description: "Learn how abstractive summarization differs from sentence selection and why shorter text still needs comparison with its source."
categories: [natural language generation, abstractive summarization, evaluation]
---

Rosa prepares the morning brief for a neighborhood archive. She receives two
service notes. Each is longer than the one sentence her colleagues need. A
shorter sentence must still preserve the source's meaning.

**Abstractive summarization** generates wording for a shorter account of a
source. The output may reuse some source phrases, but it is not limited to
selecting whole sentences. Lesson 54 used sentence selection. This lesson asks
a local language model to write a new sentence. The lesson then compares the
candidate with the original record.

::: {.callout-tip}
## What you will learn

This lesson shows how to:

- keep source records, prompts, and outputs linked to persistent IDs
- count the model's input tokens before generation
- compare generated summaries with a first-sentence baseline
- separate compression from source evidence and useful coverage
- examine names, numbers, and explicit limits without treating these checks as proof
- leave factual and editorial approval to a recorded human check.
:::

```{r}

```

## Load the local model

Course setup downloads model files before rendering at the revision recorded in
`data/nlg-models.csv`. The code below uses `huggingfaceR` to load that local
version. `R/use-nlg.R` sets offline mode. If model files are missing, the lesson
stops instead of starting a network download.

```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(huggingfaceR)
  library(purrr)
  library(reticulate)
  library(stringr)
  library(tibble)
  library(tidyr)
})

source("R/use-nlg.R")

summary_model <- load_nlg_pipeline(
  "qwen_1_5b_instruct",
  "text-generation"
)

model_record <- summary_model$metadata |>
  select(model_id, revision, license, task_scope)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false

knitr::kable(
  model_record,
  col.names = c("Model", "Revision", "License", "Course task"),
  caption = "Pinned local model used for the generated summaries",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
#| include: false

stopifnot(
  all(c(
    "dplyr", "huggingfaceR", "purrr",
    "reticulate", "stringr", "tibble", "tidyr"
  ) %in% loadedNamespaces()),
  identical(model_record$model_id, "Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct"),
  identical(
    model_record$revision,
    "989aa7980e4cf806f80c7fef2b1adb7bc71aa306"
  ),
  identical(model_record$license, "Apache-2.0")
)
```

The model card documents an instruction-tuned causal language model. That
description and license do not establish that its summaries are accurate.

## Keep the source beside the brief

The author wrote these fictional teaching records for this lesson. They are not
a random sample, a held-out benchmark, or evidence about archive services
elsewhere.

Each brief states information that matters to the reader. SUM-01 needs the
service, Tuesday schedule, and boundary on volunteer help. SUM-02 needs the
event, photo-identification rule, and restricted-storage limit.

```{r}
summary_sources <- tribble(
  ~source_id, ~brief, ~source_text,
  "SUM-01",
  paste(
    "One sentence for staff; retain the job-search service, Tuesday help",
    "schedule, and boundary on volunteer help."
  ),
  paste(
    "The Riverton library opens a new job-search room on Monday.",
    "The room has 12 computers.",
    "Volunteers offer free help on Tuesdays, but they do not complete",
    "applications for visitors.",
    "The pilot runs for six weeks."
  ),
  "SUM-02",
  paste(
    "One sentence for visitors; retain the catalog workshop,",
    "photo-identification rule, and restricted-storage limit."
  ),
  paste(
    "The neighborhood archive will open Room 5 on 14 September for a",
    "catalog workshop led by Maya Chen.",
    "Registration is free, but visitors must bring photo identification.",
    "The session does not include access to restricted storage."
  )
)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false

knitr::kable(
  summary_sources,
  col.names = c("Source ID", "Brief", "Source text"),
  caption = "Constructed source records and their summary briefs",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
#| include: false

stopifnot(
  identical(summary_sources$source_id, c("SUM-01", "SUM-02")),
  !anyDuplicated(summary_sources$source_id),
  all(str_count(summary_sources$source_text, "[.!?]") >= 3L)
)
```

## Declare required and optional facts

The author fixes the checklist before generation. A missing required item
requires candidate revision. Optional clues remain useful during source checks,
but their omission alone does not violate the brief.

```{r}
summary_checks <- tribble(
  ~source_id, ~check_id, ~needed_information, ~required, ~pattern,
  "SUM-01", "F1", "job-search service", TRUE,
  "\\bjob[ -]search\\b",
  "SUM-01", "F2", "Tuesday help", TRUE,
  "\\bTuesday\\b",
  "SUM-01", "F3", "volunteers do not complete applications", TRUE,
  "\\b(not|no|never|without|do not|does not)\\b",
  "SUM-01", "F4", "12 computers", FALSE,
  "\\b12\\b",
  "SUM-01", "F5", "six-week pilot", FALSE,
  "\\b(six|6)[ -]week",
  "SUM-02", "F6", "catalog workshop", TRUE,
  "\\bworkshop\\b",
  "SUM-02", "F7", "photo identification", TRUE,
  "\\b(photo|identification|ID)\\b",
  "SUM-02", "F8", "no restricted-storage access", TRUE,
  "\\b(not|no|without|does not)\\b",
  "SUM-02", "F9", "Room 5", FALSE,
  "\\bRoom 5\\b",
  "SUM-02", "F10", "14 September", FALSE,
  "\\b14\\b.*\\bSeptember\\b",
  "SUM-02", "F11", "Maya Chen", FALSE,
  "\\bMaya Chen\\b",
  "SUM-02", "F12", "free registration", FALSE,
  "\\bfree\\b"
)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false

knitr::kable(
  summary_checks |>
    select(source_id, check_id, needed_information, required),
  col.names = c(
    "Source ID",
    "Check",
    "Predeclared information",
    "Required by brief"
  ),
  caption = "Required facts and optional clues for source checks declared before generation",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
#| include: false

stopifnot(
  identical(summary_checks$check_id, paste0("F", 1:12)),
  all(summary_checks$source_id %in% summary_sources$source_id),
  all(summary_checks$required %in% c(TRUE, FALSE)),
  all(summary_checks$needed_information[summary_checks$required] != "")
)
```

## Examine the input limit before generation

A model token is a tokenizer unit, not necessarily a word. The prompt includes
the instruction, brief, and source text, so all three count against the input
budget. This demonstration uses a 256-token limit and prohibits truncation.

```{r}
summary_system <- paste(
  "Write one sentence for the stated brief.",
  "Use only information in the source.",
  "Do not add a cause, recommendation, or new event."
)

summary_inputs <- summary_sources |>
  mutate(
    user_prompt = paste0(
      "BRIEF: ", brief,
      "\nSOURCE ID: ", source_id,
      "\nSOURCE: ", source_text
    ),
    model_prompt = map2_chr(
      summary_system,
      user_prompt,
      \(system, user) {
        nlg_chat_prompt(
          summary_model$tokenizer,
          system,
          user
        )
      }
    ),
    input_tokens = map_int(
      model_prompt,
      \(prompt) nlg_token_count(summary_model$tokenizer, prompt)
    )
  )
```

```{r}
#| echo: false

knitr::kable(
  summary_inputs |>
    select(source_id, input_tokens),
  col.names = c("Source ID", "Complete prompt tokens"),
  caption = "Tokenizer counts before summarization",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
#| include: false

stopifnot(
  identical(nrow(summary_inputs), 2L),
  all(summary_inputs$input_tokens > 0L),
  all(summary_inputs$input_tokens <= 256L),
  all(str_detect(summary_inputs$model_prompt, "SOURCE ID"))
)
```

The workflow does not remove text to fit the limit. A longer document would
need a stated policy before the model call. Options include separate sections
or hierarchical summarization, which summarizes sections before combining their
summaries.

## Generate the candidate summaries

Greedy decoding chooses the highest-scoring next token at each step. The output
limit is 72 new tokens. The call returns the generated text and token-level
stopping information from the local model.

```{r}
summary_results <- summary_inputs |>
  mutate(
    generation = map(
      model_prompt,
      \(prompt) {
        nlg_generate(
          summary_model,
          prompt,
          max_new_tokens = 72L,
          repetition_penalty = 1.05
        )
      }
    ),
    generated_summary = map_chr(generation, "text"),
    output_tokens = map_int(generation, "output_tokens"),
    ended_by_eos = map_lgl(generation, "ended_by_eos"),
    hit_token_cap = map_lgl(generation, "hit_token_cap"),
    first_sentence_baseline = map_chr(
      str_split(source_text, "(?<=[.!?])\\s+"),
      \(sentences) sentences[[1]]
    )
  )
```

```{r}
#| echo: false

knitr::kable(
  summary_results |>
    select(source_id, generated_summary, first_sentence_baseline),
  col.names = c(
    "Source ID",
    "Generated abstractive candidate",
    "First-sentence teaching baseline"
  ),
  caption = "Generated summaries beside an extractive comparator",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
#| include: false

stopifnot(
  all(nzchar(summary_results$generated_summary)),
  all(summary_results$output_tokens > 0L),
  all(summary_results$output_tokens <= 72L),
  all(summary_results$ended_by_eos | summary_results$hit_token_cap),
  any(
    summary_results$generated_summary !=
      summary_results$first_sentence_baseline
  )
)
```

The first-sentence baseline is available before model generation. The comparison
does not match output lengths. It shows the difference between selecting source
wording and generating a new account.

## Measure shortening without calling it truth

The next table counts whitespace-separated words. That rule is easy to examine,
but it is different from the model tokenizer used for the generation budget.
A compression ratio is candidate length divided by source length. A ratio below
1 means the candidate is shorter. The ratio says nothing about whether the
candidate kept the needed facts.

```{r}
count_words <- function(text) {
  str_count(str_squish(text), "\\S+")
}

compression <- summary_results |>
  transmute(
    source_id,
    source_words = map_int(source_text, count_words),
    generated_words = map_int(generated_summary, count_words),
    first_sentence_words = map_int(
      first_sentence_baseline,
      count_words
    ),
    generated_to_source = generated_words / source_words
  )
```

```{r}
#| echo: false

knitr::kable(
  compression,
  digits = 2,
  col.names = c(
    "Source ID",
    "Source words",
    "Generated words",
    "Baseline words",
    "Generated/source ratio"
  ),
  caption = "Length diagnostics use whitespace-separated words",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
#| include: false

stopifnot(
  all(compression$source_words > compression$generated_words),
  all(compression$generated_to_source > 0),
  all(compression$generated_to_source < 1)
)
```

The model can produce a short sentence by selecting relevant content, omitting
necessary content, or both. Length cannot distinguish those cases.

## Examine facts chosen before generation

Rosa writes a checklist before reading the output. A **regular expression** is a
pattern for matching text. The expressions below find visible strings
related to that checklist. A missing match suggests a possible omission to
examine. A match does not establish the correct role or limits of a name, number,
or negative statement.

```{r}
summary_flags <- summary_checks |>
  left_join(
    summary_results |>
      select(source_id, generated_summary),
    by = "source_id"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    text_flag = str_detect(
      generated_summary,
      regex(pattern, ignore_case = TRUE)
    )
  ) |>
  select(
    source_id,
    check_id,
    needed_information,
    required,
    text_flag
  )

summary_actions <- summary_flags |>
  group_by(source_id) |>
  summarise(
    decision = list(nlg_required_fact_action(required, text_flag)),
    optional_clues_missing = sum(!required & !text_flag),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    missing_required = map_int(decision, "missing_required"),
    action = if_else(
      map_lgl(decision, "revision_needed"),
      "revise",
      "send to human source review"
    )
  ) |>
  select(
    source_id,
    missing_required,
    optional_clues_missing,
    action
  )
```

```{r}
#| echo: false

knitr::kable(
  summary_flags,
  col.names = c(
    "Source ID",
    "Check",
    "Information chosen before generation",
    "Required by brief",
    "Surface flag present"
  ),
  caption = "String-match flags for required facts and optional clues for source checks",
  row.names = FALSE
)

knitr::kable(
  summary_actions,
  col.names = c(
    "Source ID",
    "Missing required facts",
    "Missing optional clues",
    "Next action"
  ),
  caption = "Only missing required facts trigger automatic revision",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
#| include: false

stopifnot(
  identical(summary_flags$check_id, paste0("F", 1:12)),
  all(summary_flags$source_id %in% summary_sources$source_id),
  is.logical(summary_flags$text_flag),
  length(summary_flags$text_flag) == 12L,
  any(!summary_flags$text_flag),
  all(
    summary_actions$action[
      summary_actions$missing_required == 0L
    ] == "send to human source review"
  ),
  all(summary_actions$action %in% c(
    "revise",
    "send to human source review"
  ))
)
```

This check is intentionally incomplete. It cannot detect a changed relation, an
incorrect number association, a cause absent from the source, or a fluent generalization.
Those errors require comparison of the source and candidate.

Compare each summary with the volunteer and storage rules in its source.
For SUM-01, volunteers offer Tuesday help but do not complete applications for
visitors. For SUM-02, the session does not include access to restricted storage.
A general statement about limits does not preserve either rule. The string
checks can miss changes in these relationships.

N-gram overlap metrics such as ROUGE compare word sequences with a
reference under a specified normalization rule. Normalization standardizes text
before comparison. These metrics do not measure the share of claims with
evidence in the source.

## Record the limit of automated checks

Execution can establish that a model executed, stayed within the configured limits,
and returned text. It cannot grant factual or editorial approval.

```{r}
summary_review <- tibble(
  review = c(
    "local model execution",
    "prompt input within 256 tokens",
    "output stopped at EOS or token cap",
    "required-fact surface screen",
    "human checks of source evidence",
    "human checks of usefulness and prose"
  ),
  status = c(
    sprintf(
      "completed: %d candidates",
      sum(nzchar(summary_results$generated_summary))
    ),
    sprintf(
      "within budget: %d/%d candidates",
      sum(summary_inputs$input_tokens <= 256L),
      nrow(summary_inputs)
    ),
    sprintf(
      "recorded: %d/%d candidates",
      sum(summary_results$ended_by_eos | summary_results$hit_token_cap),
      nrow(summary_results)
    ),
    sprintf(
      "held: %d/%d candidates missing required facts",
      sum(summary_actions$missing_required > 0L),
      nrow(summary_actions)
    ),
    "pending",
    "pending"
  )
)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false

knitr::kable(
  summary_review,
  col.names = c("Check stage", "Status"),
  caption = "Automatic execution checks remain separate from human checks",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
#| include: false

stopifnot(
  !any(summary_review$status == "passed"),
  identical(tail(summary_review$status, 2L), c("pending", "pending"))
)
```

Before publication, a reader must compare each summary claim with its source.
The reader must find omissions of essential information. The reader must reject
additions without source evidence. A fluent one-sentence result is only a candidate.

## What to remember

- Abstractive summarization generates wording. Extractive summarization selects
  source text.
- Count the complete prompt with the model tokenizer.
- Disclose any truncation.
- Compression describes length, not coverage or source evidence.
- Examine omissions and additions against a brief written before generation.
- Names, numbers, and negation flags are prompts for human checks, not semantic proof.
- Keep model execution separate from human factual and editorial approval.
